From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Unexpected latency spikes this morning

Team — initial findings:
- No deliberate rollout recorded in the control plane between 08:30-09:30.
- Autoscaler shows a short-lived oscillation: one host group hit OOM and the scheduler moved traffic to a real-time optimized variant that is single-tenant and lacks prefix/KV caching for this model.
- The lack of persistent KV cache for that variant increases cold-kv miss penalty and multiplies tail latency under retry storms. See attached perf-log-20271009.json and p99-traces.png.

Immediate asks:
1) Product: can we disable the routed fallback to the real-time variant for ShopMosaic for the next 2 hours? This is an exceptions gate (config change).
2) SRE/Runtime: short-term mitigation = enforce sticky routing to the primary variant and enable transient in-memory prefix caching on the fallback for 1 hour if pausing is not possible.
3) PM/Eng long-term: persistent KV cache (persist across host restarts) for that variant; this needs prioritization on the roadmap.

I'll keep digging on the exact host OOM cause.

— Marcus
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime

Hi Rina / ShopMosaic team,

We’re investigating a brief service disruption affecting a small portion of checkout flows this morning. Impact window: 08:45–09:10 PT; affected requests ~3%. Root cause under investigation; initial telemetry indicates a fallback path that temporarily lacked persistent KV warming, increasing tail latency during retry bursts.

Actions taken:
- We are pausing the routed fallback to the real-time variant for your account and rebalancing traffic to the primary pool.
- Immediate mitigations applied to reduce retry amplification.
- SRE and runtime engineers are collecting traces and metrics; a post-incident summary will follow within 48 hours.

If you need an SLA exception or credits while we complete the postmortem, we can process this manually — please confirm.

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>, Rina Patel <rina@shopmosaic.com>, Anya Collins <anya.collins@shopmosaic.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2027 14:58:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Unexpected latency spikes this morning

Update + decisions: 
- We approved a temporary pause of the routed fallback for ShopMosaic (Marcus executed the rule at 14:22 PT). Metrics show error rate back to baseline within two minutes after pause.
- Short-term mitigations performed: sticky routing + transient in-memory prefix caching enabled on the real-time pool — reduced p99 by ~420ms (see p99-traces.png).
- Customer note (Marissa’s draft) approved — sending now. Rina, let us know if you want the SLA exception; we will fast-track.

Roadmap asks for leadership / PMs: 
1) Prioritize persistent KV cache for the real-time variant (owner: Marcus) — estimated 3 sprints; this should be an explicit item on the inference runtime roadmap.
2) Add a safety flag in routing policy UI to 'disable routed fallback per-account' (owner: Product) — low-effort, high-value for key customers.
3) Postmortem + KB: SRE to own 48-hour postmortem and a KB article for customers on best practices re: retries and fallback behavior.

Jonas / Evelyn: can you sync with Sales/CS about communicating the postmortem and whether credits are appropriate? I’ll open the SUP ticket and assign follow-ups.

Thanks team — Soojin
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
